summary: The study describes the fabrication of TiO2 microstructures using atomic layer deposition (ALD) on macroporous silicon templates. The process involves the controlled deposition of TiO2 on the porous silicon structure, followed by selective removal of the silicon to leave behind hollow TiO2 microstructures. The ALD process allows for uniform and conformal coating of the pores, enabling the creation of complex 3D microstructures with high surface area and porosity.
evidence: The deposition of TiO2 was performed following the work of Aarik et al. [22]. For the process a commercial reactor (Savannah100, Cambridge NanoTech Inc.) was used. The two reactants are titanium isopropoxide (Ti(OCH(CH3)2)4) and H2O. The temperature in the reaction chamber was 150°C and the half-cycle time for each precursor was chosen to be 90 s.
